nc_section_1.blurb: Section 1 is the far-left stretch of the old quarry face at Rocky Face Recreational Area, in North Carolina's Piedmont near Hiddenite. You head left from the lot along the hiking trail to reach it. It is a friendly, beginner-oriented wall with fourteen routes: about ten are bolted for lead, and four are top-rope only. Grades are mostly easy to moderate, from 5.5 up through the 5.9s, with just one 5.10 at the top end, so it suits novices and groups. Several lines can be rigged for top-rope by walking the side trail. Rock quality varies and loose pieces come off now and then, so wear a helmet, belayers included.

nc_tmi_boulder.blurb: TMI Boulder is an enormous block in the lower part of Dixon School Boulders, within Crowders Mountain in the North Carolina Piedmont. Its best-known feature is a cave that tunnels through from the front face to the back, and the block carries several highball lines. There are thirteen problems on conglomerate, all bouldering. Roughly half sit between V0 and V2, a few more land around V3 and V4, and the top end reaches V6 and V8, so there is something for most levels as long as you are comfortable with tall landings and a stack of pads.

nc_12_big_arete.blurb: Big Arete is one of the numbered climbing sections at Pilot Mountain State Park, in North Carolina's Piedmont. The routes go up a large pale quartzite block perched roughly 80 feet above the trail, just right of the Little Amphitheater, which tends to stay damp. Most of the thirteen lines are bolted sport climbs, with three top-ropes and a single trad route. The grades lean hard for a Pilot section: a few routes in the 5.6 to 5.9 range, a couple of 5.10s, and six at 5.11 or harder, including four around 5.12. A good stop for climbers working through the upper grades.

nc_masterlock_boulder.blurb: Masterlock Boulder is one of the two big blocks you meet first in the Central Area of Moore's Wall, at Hanging Rock State Park in the North Carolina Piedmont. Most of the lines are on its tall front face or on the steep side facing away from the trail. It holds thirteen boulder problems from V1 to V9: about four easy-to-moderate ones from V1 to V3, a few mid-range V4 and V5 problems, and six at V6 and above. Because the grade range is so wide, it works equally well as a warm-up stop or a full session.

nc_hanging_chain_left_field.blurb: Left Field is a cliff at Rumbling Bald in western North Carolina, roughly 300 yards left of the Hanging Chain wall. It is the most out-of-the-way of the well-developed winter areas at the Bald, and the rock is better featured and generally better quality than the main face, though some of the easy sections are weaker. Many lines have an airy feel. Of thirteen routes, twelve are trad and one is sport, with grades running from 5.9 up to 5.12 and most falling in the 5.10 to 5.11 range. Plan on a long walk in, and treat it as a cooler-weather destination.

nc_07_little_amphitheater.blurb: Little Amphitheater is a short quartzite wall at Pilot Mountain State Park in North Carolina's Piedmont. It sits left of the Three Bears gully, only a few dozen steps from where the gully drops you at the base of the cliff. This is where guides bring clients and where newcomers learn to climb, so expect company. Of thirteen routes, ten are top-ropes, two are sport and one is trad. Most are easy to moderate, roughly 5.6 to 5.8, with three 5.10s for those who want a bit more of a challenge.
